scenario: 面试官只给一句「设计一个打车 App」，不给任何规格，45 分钟内要产出可行架构。
scenario_en: The interviewer gives you one line — "design a ride-hailing app" — no spec, and 45 minutes to produce a workable architecture.
q: 系统设计面试本质上在考察什么能力？
q_en: What ability does a system design interview mainly test?
options: 把模糊的高层问题拆解成所需的基础设施组件
把面试前死记硬背的标准架构模板照搬到题目上
像编码轮那样手写不出语法错误的完整代码
记住市面上尽可能多的数据库产品名称和参数
options_en: Breaking an ambiguous, high-level problem into the infrastructure pieces it needs.
Applying a rote-memorized standard architecture template directly to whatever the prompt is.
Handwriting complete code with zero syntax errors, like a coding round.
Memorizing as many database product names and their parameters as possible.
why: 题目故意留白、规格不全，考的是你能否拆出服务、数据库、负载均衡等构件并推进出解；比算法题更贴近真实工程判断。
why_en: A system design interview mainly tests whether you can turn an ambiguous problem into the infrastructure pieces needed to solve it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Fuzzy["Fuzzy prompt"] --> Decompose["Decompose"]
    Decompose --> Parts["Services + storage"]
    Parts --> System["Working system"]
optionExplanations: 对，这正是核心能力——面试官故意把需求说得模糊，就是要看你能不能独立拆出所需的服务、存储这些构件并往前推进。
误解：模板背得再熟，遇到没见过的变体照样卡壳，面试真正看的是临场拆解，不是照搬套路。
误解：零语法错误的完整代码是编码轮的要求，设计轮通常只要接口和数据流清楚，不用抠语法。
误解：记住再多数据库产品名和参数也代替不了权衡判断，选型要靠约束推理，不是知识竞赛。
optionExplanations_en: Right — interviewers deliberately keep the prompt vague to see if you can independently break it into the services and storage you need and push forward.
Misconception: a memorized template collapses the moment the question varies; what gets tested is on-the-spot decomposition, not reciting a script.
Misconception: syntax-error-free complete code is a coding-round ask; design rounds just need clear interfaces and data flow, not syntax.
Misconception: knowing many database names and their parameters does not replace trade-off reasoning — picking one still needs constraint-driven judgment.

scenario: 你和另一位候选人做同一道「设计 Twitter」，两人架构完全不同，却都拿到了通过。
scenario_en: You and another candidate got the same "design Twitter" prompt, built completely different architectures, and both passed.
q: 关于「标准答案」，系统设计面试的正确认知是？
q_en: What is the right mindset about standard answers in system design interviews?
options: 每道题都有唯一标准答案，必须精确命中
回答内容不重要，只要讲话时间够长
很多题有多个可行答案，考官看重权衡与表达
只要猜中面试官心中的方案就能过关
options_en: Every question has one exact standard answer you must hit.
Content doesn't matter as long as you talk for a long time.
Many questions have multiple workable answers; interviewers value trade-offs and clarity.
You just need to guess the architecture the interviewer has in mind.
why: 设计面试没有唯一正解；考官评估你在复杂问题里怎么权衡取舍、怎么把思路讲清楚。
why_en: Design interviews are not about one right answer — interviewers assess how you weigh trade-offs and communicate your thinking.
optionExplanations: 误解：以为有单一标准答案，遇到题目一变体就懵，其实设计题常有多种可行解。
误解：以为靠拖时间就能过关，考官在意的是内容的推理质量，不是时长。
对，考官更看重你能不能把利弊说清楚、讲出让人信服的理由，而不是刚好蒙对某个固定答案。
误解：把面试当成猜谜游戏不可控，稳妥做法是澄清约束、自己推出合理方案。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: assuming one exact answer exists — the moment the prompt varies you get stuck, but most design prompts allow several workable solutions.
Misconception: assuming talk time matters more than content — interviewers grade the quality of your reasoning, not how long you speak.
Right — interviewers care more about whether you can lay out the trade-offs and argue for your choice than whether you land on one fixed answer.
Misconception: treating it as a guessing game is unreliable; the safer move is clarifying constraints and deriving a reasonable design yourself.

scenario: 你刷了 500 道 LeetCode，但从没独立上线过一个服务，现在要准备系统设计轮。
scenario_en: You've done 500 LeetCode problems but never shipped a service end to end, and now you have a system design round.
q: 与 LeetCode 式算法面试相比，系统设计面试的定位差异是？
q_en: How is a system design interview positioned differently from a LeetCode-style algorithm interview?
options: 更偏学术理论，脱离动手实践
像编码轮一样死抠语法对错细节
更实践、更接近日常真实工作
评估中的权重比算法轮更低
options_en: More academic and theoretical, detached from hands-on practice.
Just as syntax-picky about exact code details as a coding round.
More practical and closer to everyday engineering work.
Weighted less in the overall evaluation than the algorithms round.
why: 系统设计是实践型面试，多数工程师觉得它比刷题更贴近真实工作，考的是工程判断而非算法技巧。
why_en: System design interviews are practical and feel closer to real engineering work than LeetCode-style algorithm interviews.
tradeoff: 贴近真实工程判断 vs 贴近算法解题技巧
whenOtherWins: 若面试明确是刷题轮（考算法复杂度和边界条件），考察重点确实换成解题技巧而非架构判断。

termDefinitions.meaning: 以算法与数据结构刷题、面试练习著称的在线平台，常用来代称算法式面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LeetCode is an online platform for algorithm and data-structure practice, often used to describe algorithm-style interviews.

optionExplanations: 误解：把设计面试想成偏理论研究、脱离动手实践，其实它考的是能不能落地成可行架构。
误解：以为要像编码题一样死抠语法对错细节，系统设计其实很少纠结具体语法。
对，系统设计更贴近日常工程决策——选组件、权衡取舍，比刷算法题更像真实工作。
误解：以为权重比算法轮更低，实际上级别越高，这轮的权重往往越大，不是越小。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: treating it as academic research detached from hands-on practice — it actually tests whether you can land on a workable architecture.
Misconception: expecting it to be as syntax-picky as a coding round — system design rarely cares about exact syntax.
Right — system design mirrors day-to-day engineering decisions like picking components and weighing trade-offs, closer to real work than algorithm drills.
Misconception: assuming it's weighted less than the algorithms round — for senior roles this round is often weighted more heavily, not less.

scenario: 你在同一家公司同时投了入门、中级、高级三个岗位，想知道哪几轮会安排系统设计。
scenario_en: You applied to entry, mid, and senior openings at the same company and want to know which loops include a system design round.
q: 关于职级与系统设计面试的关系，正确的有？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about level and system design interviews are correct?
options: 入门级岗位通常没有系统设计面试（有例外）
到了中级，系统设计面试开始变得常见
高级级别基本必考，且权重格外大
职级越高，系统设计面试越不重要
options_en: Entry-level roles usually skip the system design round, with exceptions.
At mid-level, system design interviews become common.
At senior level, it is essentially mandatory and weighted heavily.
The higher the level, the less system design matters.
why: 入门级基本不考、中级渐多、高级是常态且权重不成比例地高；职级越高，系统设计信号反而越关键。
why_en: Entry-level rarely has system design, it becomes common at mid-level, and at senior level it is the norm with outsized weight.
optionExplanations: 对，入门岗大多直接跳过这一轮，但也有公司是例外，投递前最好先确认。
对，到中级这轮就变成常规环节，备考要正式把它排进计划。
对，高级岗基本必考，而且权重往往不成比例地高，是筛选的核心信号。
误解：级别越高系统设计权重不是变小反而变大，这个说法和实际相反。
optionExplanations_en: Right — entry-level roles usually skip this round, though a few companies are the exception, so it's worth confirming before you apply.
Right — at mid-level it becomes a standard part of the loop, so it belongs in serious prep plans.
Right — at senior level it is essentially mandatory and carries outsized weight as a core signal.
Misconception: the opposite is true — system design weight tends to grow, not shrink, at higher levels.

scenario: 你只剩一周备考，要把时间押在出现频率最高的那一类题上。
scenario_en: You have one week left to prep and need to bet your time on the single most common type of question.
q: 绝大多数系统设计面试属于哪一类？
q_en: What category do most system design interviews fall into?
options: 低层设计（类结构 / OOD）
前端设计
ML 系统设计
产品设计 / 基础设施设计
options_en: Low-Level Design (class structure / OOD).
Frontend design.
ML system design.
Product design / infrastructure design.
why: 压倒性多数题目是产品/基础设施设计，如设计 Uber、限流器，靠服务、负载均衡、数据库这类构件求解。
why_en: The overwhelming majority of system design interviews are product or infrastructure design questions like designing Uber or a rate limiter.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层设计：考类结构、对象与接口设计，也叫面向对象设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-Level Design (LLD) is an interview type about designing class structures, objects, and interfaces.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象设计：LLD 面试的另一个称呼。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Object-Oriented Design (OOD) is another name for the LLD interview format.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器学习，这里指以建模、特征工程为核心的系统设计面试类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ML stands for Machine Learning, referring here to the interview type centered on modeling and feature engineering.

optionExplanations: 误解：LLD 单独聚焦类和接口设计，是专门指南覆盖的题型，不属于本指南的主线范围。
误解：前端设计是独立类别，聚焦客户端状态和渲染，同样只占很小比例。
误解：ML 系统设计专攻建模和特征工程，是少数题目才会遇到的类型。
对，这类题目占了绝大多数——像打车调度或限流器这种，答案要靠服务、存储和流量分发这些基础设施构件拼出来。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: LLD focuses narrowly on class and interface design — it has its own dedicated guide, not this one.
Misconception: frontend design is a separate category about client state and rendering, and it's also a small slice.
Misconception: ML system design centers on modeling and feature engineering, which only a minority of prompts need.
Right — most prompts fall here: things like ride-hailing dispatch or a rate limiter get solved with services, storage, and traffic-distribution pieces.

scenario: 面试官要求你为停车场系统设计类结构：对象、接口、继承与方法，不涉及服务器、数据库等部署问题。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to design the class structure for a parking lot system: objects, interfaces, inheritance, and methods, with no server or database deployment concerns.
q: 这属于哪类面试，该按什么准备？
q_en: What type of interview is this, and how should you prepare?
options: 产品设计，用本指南
基础设施设计，也走本指南
低层设计LLD，走专门指南
ML系统设计，走专门指南
options_en: Product design — this guide fits.
Infrastructure design — also this guide.
Low-Level Design (LLD) — needs its own dedicated guide.
ML system design — needs the dedicated ML guide.
why: 题目在设计类结构、对象与接口，属于低层设计（LLD/OOD），备考路径要走专门的 LLD 指南，不是本指南。
why_en: Designing class structure, objects, and interfaces is a Low-Level Design interview, which needs its own dedicated LLD guide.
whenOtherWins: 若题目要求设计 Uber 后端这类画服务、数据库、负载均衡的题，才回到本指南覆盖的产品/基础设施设计。
tradeoff: 类结构与对象设计 vs 服务、数据库这类基础设施设计

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层设计：考类结构、对象与接口设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-Level Design (LLD) is an interview type about designing class structures, objects, and interfaces.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象设计：LLD 面试的另一个称呼。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Object-Oriented Design (OOD) is another name for the LLD interview format.

optionExplanations: 产品设计适合让你画服务、用户流程和后端组件的题，比如设计后端服务，这道类结构题不属于这类。
基础设施设计适合考容量、存储和流量分发的题，同样不是这道只画类和接口的题目。
对，题目在设计对象、接口和继承关系，这是 LLD/OOD 的典型信号，应该参考专门的 LLD 备考资料。
ML 系统设计适合考建模、特征工程的题，这里没有任何模型或数据管道，用不上。
optionExplanations_en: Product design fits prompts about drawing services, user flows, and backend components — not this class-structure question.
Infrastructure design fits capacity, storage, and traffic-distribution prompts, which this class-and-interface question isn't either.
Right — designing objects, interfaces, and inheritance is the classic LLD/OOD signal, so it calls for dedicated LLD prep material.
ML system design fits modeling and feature-engineering prompts — there is no model or data pipeline here to apply it to.

scenario: 面试内容包含 ML 建模、特征工程等应用机器学习工程师的核心职责，面试官会深挖模型和特征的选择。
scenario_en: The interview covers ML modeling and feature engineering — core responsibilities of applied machine learning engineers — and the interviewer will dig into model and feature choices.
q: 应按哪类面试准备？
q_en: Which interview type should you prepare for?
options: ML 系统设计，走专门的 ML 指南
产品设计，把 ML 当黑盒组件、走本指南
低层设计（LLD），走 LLD 指南
前端设计，找前端专门资源
options_en: ML system design — use the dedicated ML guide.
Product design — treat ML as a black box and use this guide.
Low-Level Design — use the LLD guide.
Frontend design — find dedicated frontend resources.
why: 题面说面试会深挖建模和特征工程，这正是 ML 系统设计的核心边界，应走专门的 ML System Design 指南。B 把 ML 当黑盒，和「深挖建模」矛盾；C 考类结构和接口，D 考客户端状态和渲染，都与本题内容无关。
why_en: The prompt says the interview digs into modeling and feature engineering, which is the core of ML system design, so prepare with the dedicated ML System Design guide. B treats ML as a black box, contradicting the deep modeling focus; C is about class structure and interfaces, D about client state and rendering — neither matches this interview.
whenOtherWins: 若 ML 只是产品里接入的黑盒组件、不深挖建模细节，那仍属于产品设计面试范畴。
tradeoff: ML 建模与特征工程能力 vs 服务/基础设施设计能力

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器学习，这里指以建模、特征工程为核心的系统设计面试类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ML stands for Machine Learning, referring here to the interview type centered on modeling and feature engineering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器学习系统设计：考建模、特征工程等应用 ML 工程能力的面试类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ML System Design is an interview type covering modeling, feature engineering, and applied ML engineering.

optionExplanations: 对，题目要深挖建模和特征工程，这是 ML 系统设计的核心边界，按 ML 系统设计专门指南来准备最合适。
错：把 ML 当黑盒组件属于产品设计，与题面「深挖建模和特征选择」矛盾。
错：LLD 考类结构、接口和类关系，这里没有类结构问题，用不上 LLD 指南。
错：前端设计考客户端状态、渲染和交互，和这里的建模、特征工程完全不搭边。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the prompt digs into modeling and feature engineering, squarely ML system design, so the dedicated ML guide is the right prep path.
Wrong: treating ML as a black-box component is product design, which contradicts the prompt's deep dive into modeling and feature choices.
Wrong: LLD covers class structure, interfaces, and relationships — there is no class design here.
Wrong: frontend design covers client state, rendering, and interaction — unrelated to the modeling and feature-engineering focus.

scenario: 你面中级岗，45 分钟里只讲透了鉴权一个模块，深度很够，但系统没有端到端闭环。
scenario_en: In a mid-level round you spent all 45 minutes going deep on auth alone, and the system never came together end to end.
q: 无论什么级别，候选人在系统设计面试中共同的底线要求是？
q_en: What baseline expectation applies to every level in a system design interview?
options: 至少说出三种消息队列
写出核心模块伪代码
把所有组件讲到源码级深度
完成一个满足需求的完整设计
options_en: Name at least three message queue products.
Write pseudocode for the core modules.
Explain every component down to source-code depth.
Deliver a complete design that satisfies the requirements.
why: 所有级别都要交付一个满足需求、能工作的完整设计；级别差异体现在深度，不是「能不能做完」。
why_en: Every level is expected to deliver a complete, working design that satisfies the requirements, with depth as the only differentiator.
optionExplanations: 误解：报菜名式列举消息队列产品和是否达标无关，考官不会按这个打分。
误解：伪代码只在少数题目里用得上，不是所有级别都要求写出来。
误解：时间根本撑不到源码级深度，级别差异体现在深挖广度而非讲到多细。
对，不管什么级别，都要先交付一个满足需求、能跑起来的完整设计，深度差异是后话。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: rattling off message-queue product names has nothing to do with passing the bar — it's not what gets scored.
Misconception: pseudocode only helps on a handful of prompts, not a universal requirement across levels.
Misconception: there is rarely enough time for source-code depth — level differences show up in how deep you go, not whether you go that deep.
Right — every level must first deliver a complete, working design that satisfies the requirements; depth is what varies after that.

scenario: 同一道「设计 Dropbox」，中级和高级候选人都画完了基础架构，各自还剩 15 分钟。
scenario_en: Same "design Dropbox" prompt: a mid-level and a senior candidate both finish the base architecture with 15 minutes to spare.
q: 同一道题，中级与高级工程师的达标表现差异主要在？
q_en: For the same prompt, what mainly separates a mid-level answer from a senior-level answer?
options: 中级可以跳过需求收集，高级才需要花时间做
高级必须比中级堆更多组件数量才算合格
中级基础覆盖广，高级快过基础换深挖时间
高级可以跳过高层设计，直接进入实现细节
options_en: Mid-level can skip requirements gathering; only senior needs to spend time on it.
Senior engineers must stack in more components than mid-level to qualify.
Mid-level covers the basics broadly; senior moves fast through basics to buy deep-dive time.
Senior engineers can skip high-level design and go straight into implementation detail.
why: 中级把基础做扎实即可；高级要迅速过完基础，把省下的时间投入 deep dive 来展示深度。
why_en: A mid-level engineer nails the fundamentals broadly, while a senior engineer moves through them quickly to leave time for deep dives.
tradeoff: 基础覆盖的广度 vs 深挖展示的深度

termDefinitions.meaning: 深挖：面试中针对某个组件展开的深度追问环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is the part of the interview where you go into depth on one specific component.

optionExplanations: 误解：需求收集是所有级别共同的起点，不是只有高级才需要认真做。
误解：组件数量不代表水平，堆砌反而会让设计显得臃肿，不是达标标准。
对，两者的差异主要在时间分配：中级把基础打牢就行，高级会压缩基础环节，把挪出来的时间用在深挖上。
误解：高层设计仍是进入细节前的共同骨架，跳过会让设计缺少导航。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: requirements gathering is the starting point at every level, not something only senior candidates need to take seriously.
Misconception: component count does not signal seniority — stacking more in just makes the design bloated, not a qualifying bar.
Right — mid-level candidates cover fundamentals thoroughly, while seniors move through them fast to spend the saved time on a deep dive.
Misconception: high-level design is still the shared skeleton before details — skipping it leaves the design without navigation.

scenario: 你面的是 staff 岗，打算照搬备考高级岗时那套 45 分钟打法。
scenario_en: You're interviewing for a staff role and plan to reuse the exact playbook you used for senior loops.
q: 关于 staff+ 级别的系统设计面试，正确的是？
q_en: What is true about staff-plus system design interviews?
options: staff 级打法不同，需按级别调整
staff 级和中高级打法完全一样，无需调整
staff 级已经不再考察系统设计能力
staff 级面试只考编码，不考架构设计
options_en: Staff-level play is different and needs its own adjustments.
Staff-level play is exactly the same as mid or senior level, no adjustment needed.
Staff level no longer tests system design ability at all.
Staff-level interviews only test coding, not architecture design.
why: staff 级面试和更低级别有实质差异，不能照搬同一套打法，要按 staff 专门指导调整策略。
why_en: Staff-level system design interviews differ substantially from lower levels, so you need to adjust your approach accordingly.

termDefinitions.meaning: Staff 及以上级别的工程师，通常要影响跨团队的技术方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Staff-plus refers to staff-level and above engineers, who are expected to influence technical direction across teams.

optionExplanations: 对，staff 级面试要求展示跨团队、更高杠杆的判断，打法和更低级别有实质差异。
误解：照搬中级/高级的套路会失分，staff 期待的信号明显更高，不是完全一样。
误解：staff+ 岗位通常更依赖系统设计信号，完全不考的情况很少见。
误解：编码只覆盖实现能力，替代不了这轮要考察的架构判断力。
optionExplanations_en: Right — staff-level interviews expect cross-team, higher-leverage judgment, substantially different from lower levels.
Misconception: reusing mid/senior tactics loses points — staff level expects a visibly stronger signal, not an identical playbook.
Misconception: staff-plus roles usually lean on system design even more, not less — skipping it entirely is rare.
Misconception: coding only covers implementation skill and cannot substitute for the architectural judgment this round tests.

q: 补全 Hello Interview 归纳的、多数公司系统设计 rubric 共有的四大主题：
q_en: Fill in the four themes that Hello Interview identifies as common across most companies' system design rubrics:
text: 四大评估主题：{{Problem Navigation}} 问题导航、{{Solution Design}} 方案设计、{{Technical Excellence}} 技术卓越、{{Communication}} 沟通与协作。
why: 各公司 rubric 措辞不同，但多数都能归到这四件事上（这是 Hello Interview 的归纳框架）；准备时可对照这四项逐一自查。
why_en: Company rubrics are worded differently, but most map onto these four themes (a framework distilled by Hello Interview): problem navigation, solution design, technical excellence, and communication and collaboration.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Rubric["Rubric"] --> Nav["Navigation"]
    Rubric --> Sol["Solution"]
    Rubric --> Tech["Technical"]
    Rubric --> Comm["Communication"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 问题导航：把模糊问题拆解、排优先级并推进到解的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem Navigation is the ability to decompose an ambiguous problem, prioritize it, and drive it toward a solution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 方案设计：用核心概念解决拆出的子问题，并拼成协调的整体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Solution Design means solving each subproblem with core concepts and assembling them into a coherent whole.

termDefinitions.meaning: 技术卓越：了解现行技术与公认模式，并能应用到问题上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Technical Excellence is knowing current technologies and recognized patterns and applying them to the problem at hand.

termDefinitions.meaning: 沟通与协作：能讲清概念、接住反馈、并与面试官协作解题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Communication and Collaboration means explaining ideas clearly, receiving feedback, and working with the interviewer to solve the problem.

scenario: 面试官只说「设计一个通知系统」，需求、规模、渠道全没说，你得先决定从哪下手。
scenario_en: The interviewer only says "design a notification system" — no requirements, scale, or channels — and you must decide where to start.
q: 「问题导航（Problem Navigation）」考察的核心是？
q_en: What is the core skill tested by Problem Navigation?
options: 还没理清需求就先尽快画出最终架构图
拆小问题、排优先级、推进到解
靠不断多问问题来拖延，占用面试时间
花时间证明题目本身出得有问题
options_en: Rush to draw the final architecture diagram before requirements are even clear.
Decompose the problem, prioritize, and drive toward a solution.
Stall by asking a stream of questions that just eat into interview time.
Spend time arguing the question itself is flawed.
why: 面试官想看你能否拆解、排序、推进一个规格不全的问题；这常是整场最重要、最拉开差距的一环。
why_en: Problem navigation means decomposing an under-specified problem, prioritizing it, and driving it toward a solution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 问题导航：把模糊问题拆解、排优先级并推进到解的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem Navigation is the ability to decompose an ambiguous problem, prioritize it, and drive toward a solution.

optionExplanations: 误解：架构图适合放在需求和优先级理清楚之后画，需求都没理清就先画容易返工。
对，考官想看你能不能把规格不全的问题拆解、排序、并持续往前推进到方案。
误解：提问只有服务于决策时才算导航，纯粹拖时间占用面试时长不会加分。
误解：就算题目有瑕疵，也要澄清约束继续推进，而不是花时间纠结题目本身。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the diagram belongs after requirements and priorities are clear — drawing it before that is settled often means redoing work.
Right — interviewers want to see you decompose the under-specified problem, prioritize it, and keep driving toward a solution.
Misconception: questions only count as navigation when they drive a decision — stalling with questions just to eat time does not score points.
Misconception: even with an imperfect prompt, the move is to clarify constraints and keep going, not spend time arguing the prompt itself is flawed.

scenario: 45 分钟里你花了 30 分钟纠结数据库选型，最后没画出端到端的系统。
scenario_en: You burned 30 of your 45 minutes agonizing over the database choice and never produced an end-to-end system.
q: 问题导航维度的常见失败方式有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are common failure modes in the Problem Navigation dimension?
options: 对问题探索不足、需求收集不充分
把时间花在琐碎无趣的部分而不是最重要的部分
卡死在某一块上无法向前推进
使用了过时的技术选型
options_en: Under-exploring the problem and not gathering enough requirements.
Spending time on trivial parts instead of the important ones.
Getting stuck on one piece and unable to move forward.
Choosing outdated technology.
why: 第四种被点名的失败是没能交付一个能工作的系统；用过时技术属于技术卓越维度，不算导航失败。
why_en: Common navigation failures are under-exploring requirements, focusing on trivial parts, and getting stuck; outdated tech choices belong to a different competency.
optionExplanations: 对，前期探索不够会让后续设计建立在不完整的理解上，是导航失败的典型表现。
对，优先级错位会让琐碎细节挤占关键路径的时间，也算导航失败。
对，卡在一处又没有备选推进路线，会拖垮整场面试的节奏。
误解：技术选型过时属于技术卓越维度的问题，不算作问题导航的失败。
optionExplanations_en: Right — under-exploring the problem upfront leaves the later design resting on an incomplete understanding, a classic navigation failure.
Right — bad prioritization lets trivial details crowd out time for the critical path, also a navigation failure.
Right — getting stuck with no fallback path drags down the pace of the whole interview.
Misconception: outdated technology choices belong to the technical-excellence dimension, not a navigation failure.

scenario: 你在面试里反复跳回已经讨论过的模块，时间过半仍说不清下一步该做什么。
scenario_en: You keep jumping back to parts you already covered, and halfway through you still cannot say what comes next.
q: 许多候选人在面试中无法推进，最常见的根因是？
q_en: What is the most common root cause when candidates cannot make progress in a design interview?
options: 英文技术词汇量不够，表达跟不上思路
缺乏结构化方法，没有跑道
面试官在这道题上故意刁难、连续施压
这道题目内容明显超出常规准备范围
options_en: Not enough English technical vocabulary, so expression can't keep up with the thinking.
No structured method — no track to run on.
The interviewer is deliberately being harsh and piling on pressure for this specific question.
This particular question is clearly beyond the normal scope of preparation.
why: 缺结构会让你把时间烧在错的问题上；缓解办法是跟随 Delivery Framework，给自己一条固定跑道。
why_en: Most candidates stall because they lack structure, which a delivery framework fixes by giving them a track to run on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 交付框架：给面试推进提供固定步骤的方法论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Delivery Framework is a step-by-step method that gives you a track to run on during the interview.

optionExplanations: 误解：词汇量会影响表达流畅度，但通常不是推进失败的根因。
对，没有结构化方法时，模糊的题目很容易让人跑偏或原地卡住。
误解：考官刻意刁难、持续施压的情况其实很少见，不是常见根因。
误解：多数题目其实在合理范围内，超出常规准备很少是真正的卡壳原因。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: vocabulary affects delivery fluency, but it is rarely the root cause of stalling.
Right — without a structured method, an ambiguous prompt easily makes you drift or freeze.
Misconception: interviewers deliberately piling on pressure is actually rare, not a common cause.
Misconception: most prompts are reasonably scoped — going beyond normal preparation is rarely the real culprit.

scenario: 需求已经澄清完，接下来 25 分钟你要把「设计 Ticketmaster」变成一套连贯架构。
scenario_en: Requirements are settled, and you have 25 minutes to turn "design Ticketmaster" into one coherent architecture.
q: 「方案设计（Solution Design）」维度考察什么？
q_en: What does the Solution Design dimension evaluate?
options: 背熟所有云厂商的具体服务名称清单
架构图画得多美观、排版多整齐
讲解时的台风气场与语调抑扬顿挫
用核心概念逐块求解并拼成整体
options_en: Memorizing the exact service names of every cloud vendor's product lineup.
How aesthetically pleasing and neatly laid out the diagram looks.
Stage presence, energy, and vocal cadence while presenting.
Solving each piece with core concepts and assembling a coherent whole.
why: 拆完问题后，考官看你怎么用核心概念逐块求解，且各块能拼成连贯系统，而不是零件堆砌。
why_en: Solution design assesses whether you can solve each piece with core concepts and fit the pieces into a cohesive whole.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Problem["Subproblems"] --> Concepts["Core concepts"]
    Concepts --> Blocks["Components"]
    Blocks --> Whole["Coherent system"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 方案设计：用核心概念解决拆出的子问题并拼成整体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Solution Design means solving each subproblem with core concepts and assembling them into a coherent whole.

optionExplanations: 误解：服务名只有在能解释取舍时才有价值，背熟清单本身没意义。
误解：图形排版整齐能帮助沟通，但不能替代架构逻辑本身。
误解：讲解台风与语调属于沟通维度，不属于方案设计要考的内容。
对，方案设计看的是你能不能用核心工具把每块子问题都解决掉，再让这些解法互相咬合成一个整体，而不是各管一段。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: service names only matter when you can explain the trade-off behind them — memorizing the exact lineup alone doesn't help.
Misconception: a neat, aesthetically pleasing layout can aid communication, but it can't substitute for sound architecture logic.
Misconception: presentation energy and vocal cadence belong to the communication dimension, not what solution design evaluates.
Right — after decomposing the problem, the interviewer watches whether you solve each piece with core concepts and assemble a coherent whole.

scenario: 你的白板上组件越加越多、连线越来越乱，全程没提过任何扩容或性能数字。
scenario_en: Your whiteboard keeps sprouting boxes with tangled arrows, and you haven't mentioned scaling or performance numbers once.
q: 方案设计维度的常见失败方式有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are common failure modes in the Solution Design dimension?
options: 核心概念功底不足，撑不起方案
忽略扩展性与性能问题
『意大利面设计』：结构混乱、难以理解
过早向面试官确认需求
options_en: Fundamentals too weak to support the design.
Ignoring scaling and performance considerations.
A "spaghetti design" — tangled and hard to follow.
Confirming requirements with the interviewer too early.
why: 三大失败是基础不牢、无视 scaling/性能、结构混乱的意大利面设计；确认需求恰恰是好行为。
why_en: Solution design fails through weak fundamentals, ignoring scaling and performance, or a tangled spaghetti design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 组件关系混乱、难以理解的设计，即英文说的 spaghetti design。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A spaghetti design is a system whose components are tangled together and hard to follow.

optionExplanations: 对，核心概念弱时，任何组件选择一被追问就容易露馅。
对，流量和数据增长明确时还不谈扩展性，系统就扛不住真实压力。
对，组件关系混乱到考官都跟不上，就是典型的意大利面设计。
误解：提前对齐需求属于良好的沟通行为，反而会帮助方案设计站得住脚。
optionExplanations_en: Right — with weak fundamentals, any component choice tends to fall apart under follow-up questions.
Right — when traffic or data growth is stated, ignoring scaling means the system can't handle real load.
Right — when component relationships are so tangled the interviewer can't follow, that's a textbook spaghetti design.
Misconception: confirming requirements early is good collaboration and actually strengthens the solution, not a failure.

scenario: 你一开口就报出一整套 Uber 架构，用词几乎和网上范文一样。
scenario_en: You immediately rattle off a complete Uber architecture, almost word for word from a popular write-up.
q: 面试官怀疑你在背答案时，通常会怎么做？
q_en: What will interviewers usually do if they suspect you are reciting a memorized answer?
options: 当场直接结束面试，不再继续这一轮
换成更简单基础的题目来重新测试
追问推理、故意质疑、要求讲权衡
直接跳过这一部分，不再追问细节
options_en: End the interview on the spot and not continue this round.
Switch to an easier, more basic question to retest you.
Probe your reasoning, express doubt, and ask you to walk through trade-offs.
Skip this section entirely and stop probing further.
why: 考官对背题高度警觉，会 probe 推理、故意表示怀疑、要你讲 trade-off；只有扎实基本功才顶得住。
why_en: Interviewers test for memorized answers by probing your reasoning, expressing doubt, and asking you to walk through trade-offs.
optionExplanations: 误解：只有严重违规时才会直接终止整轮面试，背答案通常只是被追问，不会当场结束。
误解：换成更简单的题目验证不了你是否真的会推理，考官不会这样处理。
对，考官会 probe 你的推理、故意表示怀疑、要你讲权衡，只有真懂才能扛住。
误解：直接跳过、不再追问会漏掉考官最想验证的推理信号，不符合常见流程。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: only serious issues end the whole interview outright — a memorized answer usually just gets probed, not ended on the spot.
Misconception: switching to an easier question can't test whether you can actually reason, so interviewers don't do this.
Right — interviewers probe your reasoning, push back on purpose, and ask you to walk through trade-offs; only real understanding survives that.
Misconception: skipping the section and dropping further probes would miss exactly the reasoning signal the interviewer is trying to verify.

scenario: 需求是写入 100k QPS，且消息不能丢、下游不能重复生效（at-least-once 投递 + 幂等消费），你必须点名具体的队列与存储方案。
scenario_en: The requirement is 100k writes per second with no message loss and no duplicate side effects downstream (at-least-once delivery plus idempotent consumers), and you have to name the actual queue and storage choices.
q: 「技术卓越（Technical Excellence）」维度考察什么？
q_en: What does the Technical Excellence dimension evaluate?
options: 懂现行技术与公认模式并能应用
背熟每种硬件型号的具体参数指标
能手写汇编级别的性能优化代码
熟悉面试官所在公司的内部专属工具
options_en: Knowing current technologies and recognized patterns, and applying them.
Memorizing the exact specs of every specific hardware model.
Being able to hand-write assembly-level performance-optimized code.
Being familiar with the internal, company-specific tools at the interviewer's employer.
why: 要设计出好系统，需要知道现在有哪些技术、有哪些公认模式（例如 at-least-once + 幂等消费来避免重复生效），并能把它们落到手头问题上。
why_en: Technical excellence means knowing current technologies and recognized patterns — such as at-least-once delivery with idempotent consumers to avoid duplicate effects — and applying them to the problem at hand.

termDefinitions.meaning: 技术卓越：了解现行技术与公认模式，并能应用到问题上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Technical Excellence is knowing current technologies and recognized patterns and applying them to the problem at hand.

optionExplanations: 对，好设计得先摸清楚当下有哪些可用技术和被验证过的模式，再把它们套到眼前这道题的约束上。
误解：硬件参数只有在影响容量估算时才需要粗略了解，不用背到具体型号细节。
误解：汇编级优化代码属于性能工程范畴，不是系统设计轮的考察重点。
误解：面试官所在公司的内部专属工具对不同背景的候选人不公平，不该成为门槛。
optionExplanations_en: Right — good design starts with knowing what technologies and proven patterns exist now, then mapping them onto the constraints in front of you.
Misconception: hardware parameters only matter as rough capacity anchors, not something you need memorized down to the specific model.
Misconception: hand-written assembly-level optimization belongs to performance engineering, not what a design round is testing.
Misconception: knowledge of the interviewer's own company-internal tools would be unfair across candidates and should not be a bar.

scenario: 你能背出 Kafka 和 Cassandra 的特性，但被问「这道题该用哪个、为什么」时卡住了。
scenario_en: You can recite Kafka and Cassandra features, but you freeze when asked which one this problem needs and why.
q: 技术卓越维度的常见失败方式有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are common failure modes in the Technical Excellence dimension?
options: 不知道有哪些可用的现行技术
用过时的方法、被十年前的硬件约束框住
识别不出常见模式与最佳实践
没有背出具体云服务的定价
options_en: Not knowing what current technologies are available.
Using outdated approaches bound by decade-old hardware limits.
Failing to recognize common patterns and best practices.
Not having memorized specific cloud pricing.
why: 还有一种失败是知道技术却不会应用到手头问题；背云服务定价从来不是考点。
why_en: Failures include not knowing available technologies, reasoning from outdated hardware constraints, and not recognizing common patterns.
optionExplanations: 对，不知道有哪些可用技术，方案选择的空间一开始就变窄了。
对，用十年前的硬件假设做决策，容量和延迟判断都会被带偏。
对，认不出常见模式时，知道积木也拼不出可靠方案。
误解：云服务定价从来不是评估内容，顶多在做成本模型时粗略估计。
optionExplanations_en: Right — not knowing which technologies are available narrows the solution space from the start.
Right — reasoning from decade-old hardware assumptions distorts your capacity and latency judgment.
Right — without recognizing common patterns, you know the pieces but can't assemble a reliable design.
Misconception: cloud pricing was never part of the evaluation, at most a rough input for a cost model.

scenario: 你用一份 2015 年的系统设计资料备考，按里面的单机容量假设估算服务器数量。
scenario_en: You're prepping from a 2015 system design guide and sizing servers with its per-machine capacity assumptions.
q: 沿用 2015 年前后的老系统设计材料，最大的风险是？
q_en: What is the main risk of relying on system design material from around 2015?
options: 材料内容量太大，根本学不完
按过时硬件假设做决策，显陈旧
面试官大概率根本不认识这些老技术
完全没风险，经典内容从不过时
options_en: There's simply too much material to get through.
Decisions rest on outdated hardware assumptions and look stale.
The interviewer most likely won't even recognize these old technologies.
No risk at all — classic content never goes stale.
why: 硬件这十年进步巨大，老材料的容量/延迟假设已失效；要用最新的 numbers to know 校准决策。
why_en: Hardware has advanced enormously in the last decade, so reasoning from outdated constraints makes your design choices look stale.
optionExplanations: 误解：内容量大只影响学习计划安排，不是老材料本身的风险。
对，过去十年硬件突飞猛进，旧教材里对容量和延迟的假设早就不成立了，照着老数字做设计选择自然显得脱节。
误解：考官通常会跟着技术进步走，大概率仍然认识这些老技术，不太可能不认识。
误解：经典概念可以复用，但数字类的约束必须重新校准，不是完全没风险。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: too much content only affects your study schedule, not a risk of the old material itself.
Right — hardware has advanced enormously in a decade, so stale capacity and latency assumptions make your design choices look outdated.
Misconception: interviewers usually keep up with newer technology and are quite likely to still recognize these older ones.
Misconception: classic concepts do transfer, but numeric constraints need recalibrating — so it is not risk-free.

scenario: 面试官全程和你在同一块白板上讨论，中途几次提出替代方案让你回应。
scenario_en: The interviewer works the same whiteboard with you and keeps floating alternative approaches for you to react to.
q: 「沟通与协作」维度实质上在评估什么？
q_en: What does the Communication and Collaboration dimension really evaluate?
options: 讲话时的台风气场与语调节奏
讲清概念、接反馈、协作解题
非母语候选人的外语表达流利度
在白板上画出架构图的速度快慢
options_en: Stage presence, energy, and vocal rhythm while speaking.
Explaining ideas clearly, taking feedback, and collaborating to solve the problem.
How fluently a non-native speaker expresses themselves in a foreign language.
How fast you can draw the architecture diagram on the whiteboard.
why: 技术面试也是同事体验预演：考官看你能否清晰表达、接住反馈、和他协作把问题解掉。
why_en: The communication dimension gauges what you'd be like as a colleague: explaining ideas, taking feedback, and collaborating on the problem.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Explain["Explain"] --> Feedback["Receive feedback"]
    Feedback --> Adjust["Adjust design"]
    Adjust --> Shared["Shared solution"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 能讲清概念、接住反馈、并与面试官协作解题的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Communication and Collaboration means explaining ideas clearly, taking feedback, and working with the interviewer to solve the problem.

optionExplanations: 误解：演讲台风与语调能加分，但代替不了协作解题本身。
对，考官在看你能不能讲清概念、接住反馈、并和他协作把问题解掉——这是同事体验的预演。
误解：非母语表达可以慢一点，逻辑清楚比流利度更重要。
误解：白板画图速度只有在拖慢沟通时才会影响体验，不是核心评分点。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: presentation energy and rhythm can help, but they can't substitute for actually collaborating on the problem.
Right — this dimension previews what you'd be like as a colleague: explaining ideas clearly, taking feedback, and solving the problem together.
Misconception: non-native delivery can be slower — clear logic matters more than fluency.
Misconception: whiteboard-drawing speed only matters if it slows the conversation down, not a core scoring point.

scenario: 面试官指出你的分片键有问题，你花了十分钟解释自己为什么没错。
scenario_en: The interviewer points out a problem with your shard key, and you spend ten minutes explaining why you are right.
q: 沟通协作维度的常见失败方式有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are common failure modes in the Communication and Collaboration dimension?
options: 讲不清楚复杂概念
收到反馈时变得防御、跟面试官争辩
陷进细节泥潭，无法与面试官协作推进
主动和面试官对齐优先级
options_en: Can't clearly explain complex concepts.
Gets defensive and argues when given feedback.
Gets lost in the weeds and can't collaborate forward.
Proactively aligns priorities with the interviewer.
why: 表达不清、反馈激起防御心、迷失在细节里，是沟通维度的三大失败；主动对齐优先级恰恰是加分项。
why_en: Communication failures include unclear explanations, getting defensive about feedback, and getting lost in the weeds instead of collaborating.
optionExplanations: 对，概念讲不清时，考官没法信任后面的设计推进。
对，被反馈触发防御或争辩，会让协作体验迅速变差。
对，陷在细节里走不出来，会挤掉和考官一起往前推进方案的时间。
误解：主动对齐优先级是良好协作的表现，反而会减少误解、加快推进。
optionExplanations_en: Right — when concepts aren't clear, the interviewer can't trust the design that follows.
Right — getting defensive or arguing over feedback quickly hurts the collaboration.
Right — getting stuck in detail crowds out the time needed to move the design forward together.
Misconception: proactively aligning priorities is good collaboration and speeds progress, not a failure mode.

scenario: 你选了单主库，面试官问「写入扛得住吗」，但并没有说你错了。
scenario_en: You picked a single primary database and the interviewer asks "will writes hold up?" without saying you are wrong.
q: 面试官对你的设计提出质疑，最好的反应是？
q_en: What is the best response when the interviewer challenges your design?
options: 无论对方怎么说都坚守原方案、寸步不让
不管理由是否成立，立刻全盘推翻设计
全程沉默不语，被动等待面试官提示
当作协作试探，回应并解释调整理由
options_en: Hold the original design firmly no matter what the interviewer says.
Immediately abandon the entire design regardless of whether the objection actually holds up.
Stay completely silent and passively wait for the interviewer to hint further.
Treat it as collaboration: respond, adjust if needed, and explain your reasoning.
why: 防御与争辩是沟通维度被点名的失败项；质疑常是在测试推理或给提示，接住反馈才是加分姿态。
why_en: Treat pushback as collaboration — respond to the feedback and adjust your design with reasons instead of getting defensive.
optionExplanations: 误解：只有确认质疑站不住脚时才该坚持，不管对方说什么都不让步会显得听不进反馈。
误解：全盘推翻只适合确认核心假设确实错了的情况，不该不问理由就默认这样反应。
误解：全程沉默、被动等提示只适合短暂停顿思考，不能当作对质疑的正式回应。
对，把质疑当协作输入，回应、按需调整并解释理由，才能展示推理力和开放度。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: only hold your ground once you've confirmed the pushback is wrong — refusing to budge no matter what reads as not listening.
Misconception: a full reset fits only when a core assumption really is wrong, not a default reaction regardless of whether the objection holds up.
Misconception: staying completely silent and passively waiting is fine for a brief pause but is not a real response to pushback.
Right — treat pushback as collaborative input: respond, adjust if needed, and explain your reasoning, showing both conviction and openness.

scenario: 面试前你读完了全部章节和范例，却一次都没有从零口头讲过一道题。
scenario_en: Before the interview you read every chapter and worked example, but never once talked through a problem from scratch out loud.
q: 「看了大量材料但从不动手练」的典型下场是？
q_en: What usually happens if you read a lot but never practice applying the material?
options: 真上场应用知识时卡壳
知识反而更牢固
对结果毫无影响
面试难度自动降低
options_en: Freezes up when it's time to actually apply the knowledge.
Knowledge actually becomes more solid.
Has no effect on the outcome at all.
The interview automatically gets easier.
why: 这是被点名的常见失败：吸收很多、应用不出来；要靠 worked solutions 和模拟练习把知识转成能上场的输出。
why_en: A common failure mode is consuming lots of material but stumbling when it's time to apply it, which only practice fixes.
optionExplanations: 对，只读不练时知识变不成输出，真上场会在应用这一步卡住。
误解：知识变牢通常靠提取练习，被动阅读反而记不住多少。
误解：准备方式会直接影响能否把知识转成口头设计，不是毫无影响。
误解：面试难度不会因为你练得少就自动下降。
optionExplanations_en: Right — reading without practicing means the knowledge never turns into output, so you freeze up applying it live.
Misconception: retention usually comes from retrieval practice — passive reading alone sticks far less.
Misconception: how you prepare directly affects whether knowledge turns into a spoken design, so it is not a non-factor.
Misconception: interview difficulty does not drop just because you practiced less.

scenario: 你此前完全没接触过系统设计，面试大约在一个月后。你要按本课程的建议规划这段时间怎么分配学习。
scenario_en: You have never studied system design and your interview is about a month away. You want to plan the time following this course's guidance.
q: 系统设计完全零基础的候选人，建议的准备节奏是？
q_en: What preparation pace is recommended for someone completely new to system design?
options: 一两天速成
至少半年
全职冲刺或摊开3-4周
无法准备，全凭经验
options_en: Cram it in one or two days.
At least six months.
A dedicated sprint, or spread over three to four weeks.
Can't be prepared for — it's all down to experience.
why: 本课程建议零基础的人做一次全职冲刺，或把准备摊开到 3-4 周；面试在一个月后，正好落在这个节奏里。一两天来不及建立框架，「至少半年」超出了可用时间。已有经验的人一周内备好也很常见。
why_en: This course suggests a dedicated sprint or three to four weeks for someone new to system design; with the interview a month out, that pace fits. One or two days is too short to build the framework, and "at least six months" exceeds the time available. Experienced candidates often prepare in under a week.
optionExplanations: 一两天顶多够刷个概览，零基础想扎实建立框架和核心概念，这个节奏来不及。
半年更像是没有明确截止日期时的从容节奏，面试通常等不了这么久，会拖慢投递进度。
对，零基础比较现实的是全职集中冲刺，或者拆成 3-4 周稳步推进，足够覆盖框架、技术和核心概念。
经验能替代一部分刷题量，但完全不做主动准备，零基础的人大概率会在框架和术语上卡住。
optionExplanations_en: One or two days is barely enough for a skim — building the framework and core concepts from zero needs more runway than that.
Six months fits a wide-open timeline with no real deadline; most interview processes can't wait that long, so it stalls momentum.
Right — for zero background, a realistic pace is a dedicated sprint or spreading it over three to four weeks, enough to cover the framework, key tech, and core concepts.
Experience can substitute for some drilling, but skipping deliberate prep entirely usually leaves a true beginner stuck on framework and terminology.

scenario: 面试排在 5 天后，你对照清单发现 Key Technologies 和 Core Concepts 两大块还完全没碰过，几天内补不完；招聘官之前提过日期可以调整。
scenario_en: The interview is 5 days away. Checking your list, you realize you haven't touched Key Technologies or Core Concepts at all and can't cover them in a few days; the recruiter mentioned earlier that the date is flexible.
q: 最合理的第一步是？
q_en: What is the most reasonable first step?
options: 硬着头皮按期上场
直接放弃这家公司
请招聘官把面试往后推
前夜通宵突击材料
options_en: Push through and interview on the original date anyway.
Give up on this company entirely.
Ask the recruiter to push the interview date back.
Pull an all-nighter cramming before the interview.
why: 缺口是两整块、几天补不完，而且招聘官明确说过日期可调，所以第一步是主动请求推迟，换来系统准备的时间。很多招聘官更在意你通过的可能性而不是原定日期；但如果只是差查漏补缺，按期上场同样合理。
why_en: The gap is two whole areas you can't close in a few days, and the recruiter said the date is flexible, so the first step is to ask for a later date. Many recruiters care more about your chance of passing than the original slot; if you only needed light review, keeping the date would be fine.
whenOtherWins: 若基础扎实、只差查漏补缺，按期面试完全合理，不必推迟。
tradeoff: 用一次沟通换更充分的准备时间 vs 按原计划上场应对不确定性

termDefinitions.meaning: 招聘方的招聘协调人，负责面试流程和岗位信息沟通。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recruiter is the hiring-side contact who coordinates the interview process and can share role expectations.

optionExplanations: 基础明显不足时硬着头皮上场，只会带着仓促感进场、放大失败概率。
放弃只适合岗位已经不再匹配的情况，光是准备不够就放弃太可惜。
对，缺口是两整块、几天补不完，招聘官又说过日期可调，主动申请推迟换更充分的准备是合理的第一步。
通宵突击只适合轻量复盘，补不了系统性的知识缺口，反而会疲劳影响发挥。
optionExplanations_en: Pushing through while clearly underprepared just means walking in rushed, which raises your odds of failing.
Giving up only makes sense once the role is no longer a fit — quitting just because you're behind on prep is premature.
Right — the gap is two whole areas you can't close in days and the recruiter said the date is flexible, so asking to push it back for real prep time is the sensible first step.
An all-nighter only works for light review; it can't close a systemic knowledge gap and leaves you tired instead.

scenario: 距离面试只剩几天，时间只够覆盖一小部分材料。
scenario_en: You only have a few days before the interview, and there is time to cover only a small slice of the material.
q: 时间最紧时的学习优先级是？
q_en: What should you prioritize when preparation time is extremely tight?
options: 把每一篇问题拆解文章都精读一遍
先框架、再略读技术、后补概念
只背熟三道经典题的标准答案
把全部时间都用来刷算法题
options_en: Deeply study every single problem-breakdown article one by one.
Learn the delivery framework first, skim key technologies, then cover core concepts.
Memorize the standard answers to just three classic questions.
Spend all the available time drilling algorithm problems.
why: 极限时间下：交付框架给你答题跑道收益最高，关键技术略读认积木，剩余时间补核心概念深度。
why_en: If you're really short on time, master the delivery framework first, skim the key technologies, and spend the rest on core concepts.
whenOtherWins: 时间充足（3-4 周）时应按顺序完整过指南并配合大量练习，而不是只抓框架。
tradeoff: 先建立答题结构 vs 先积累知识深度
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Time["Very little time"] --> Framework["Delivery framework"]
    Framework --> Tech["Skim key tech"]
    Tech --> Concepts["Core concepts"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 交付框架：给面试推进提供固定步骤的方法论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Delivery Framework is a step-by-step method that gives you a track to run on during the interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关键技术：当前主流、可直接用于设计的技术清单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the current, widely used technologies you can apply directly in your design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 核心概念：缓存、分片等构成系统设计答案的基础知识模块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the foundational building blocks, like caching and sharding, used to answer design questions.

optionExplanations: 误解：精读每一篇拆解文章确实有用，但时间根本不够，知道怎么拆却拼不出完整方案。
对，时间极紧时先拿到答题结构收益最高，再快速认识可用技术，剩下时间补概念深度。
误解：只背熟三道经典题遇到变体就无招可用，考官也很擅长识破背答案。
误解：算法练习适合编码轮，解决不了系统设计要交付完整架构的诉求。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: deeply reading every breakdown article one by one is useful, but there's not enough time — you'd know how to decompose without being able to assemble an answer.
Right — with very little time, structure first pays off most, then a fast pass on usable tech, then whatever is left on core concepts.
Misconception: memorizing three classic answers falls apart the moment the question varies, and interviewers are good at spotting recitation.
Misconception: algorithm drills fit coding rounds; they don't address the need to deliver a full architecture in a design round.

q: 把「时间极紧时的备考优先级」按先后排序：
q_en: Order the study priorities when preparation time is extremely tight:
steps: 剩余时间投入 Core Concepts（补概念深度）
先掌握 Delivery Framework（先有答题跑道）
略读 Key Technologies（认识可用积木）
why: 框架决定 50 分钟怎么花、收益最高所以先学；再认积木，最后用剩余时间补概念深度。
why_en: Learn the delivery framework first for structure, then skim the key technologies, and spend any remaining time on core concepts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 交付框架：给面试推进提供固定步骤的方法论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Delivery Framework is a step-by-step method that gives you a track to run on during the interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关键技术：当前主流、可直接用于设计的技术清单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the current, widely used technologies you can apply directly in your design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 核心概念：缓存、分片等构成系统设计答案的基础知识模块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the foundational building blocks, like caching and sharding, used to answer design questions.

q: 把「缺乏结构如何导致面试失败、又如何自救」排成因果顺序：
q_en: Put the causal chain in order: how lack of structure causes interview failure and how to recover:
steps: 把时间烧在错误的问题上，交不出完整系统
题目天生模糊、规格不全
缓解：跟随 Delivery Framework，给自己一条固定跑道
缺乏结构化的推进方法
why: 模糊问题 + 缺结构 → 时间烧错地方、交付失败；缓解 = 用交付框架当轨道跑。
why_en: An ambiguous problem plus no structure burns time on the wrong things and fails to deliver, which the delivery framework prevents.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["模糊、规格不全的问题"] --> B["缺乏结构化方法"] B --> C["时间烧错地方
交不出完整系统"] C --> M["缓解：Delivery Framework"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 交付框架：给面试推进提供固定步骤的方法论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Delivery Framework is a step-by-step method that gives you a track to run on during the interview.

q: 补全问题导航的正确姿势：
q_en: Fill in the correct Problem Navigation posture:
text: 把复杂问题{{拆解}}成更小、可管理的部分，按{{重要性}}排出优先级，并最终交付一个{{能工作}}的系统。
why: 拆解、排序、交付——这三步就是 Problem Navigation 的评分点，漏任何一步都算导航失败。
why_en: Good problem navigation means decomposing the problem, prioritizing the most important pieces, and delivering a working system.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    D["Decompose"] --> P["Prioritize"]
    P --> M["Move forward"]
    M --> W["Working design"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模糊问题拆解、排优先级并推进到解的能力，即 Problem Navigation。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem Navigation is the ability to decompose an ambiguous problem, prioritize it, and drive toward a solution.

scenario: 你按 Hello Interview「System Design in a Hurry」准备，只剩一个晚上复习它列出的四大评估维度，想把时间压在该指南认为最拉分、新手最容易栽的那一项上。
scenario_en: You're preparing with Hello Interview's "System Design in a Hurry" and have one evening to review its four evaluation themes; you want to spend it on the one that guide calls the most important and hardest for beginners.
q: 该指南的四大评估主题中，被点名「往往最重要、新手最容易栽」的是？
q_en: Among that guide's four evaluation themes, which one does it call often the most important and hardest for beginners?
options: 技术卓越
沟通与协作
方案设计
问题导航
options_en: Technical Excellence.
Communication and Collaboration.
Solution Design.
Problem Navigation.
why: Hello Interview 的指南点名 Problem Navigation 常是整场最重要、新手最挣扎的部分：导航失败会烧错时间。这是该指南的判断，不同公司的 rubric 权重可能不同，其它三项同样会被评分。
why_en: Hello Interview's guide calls Problem Navigation often the most important competency and the one newcomers struggle with most, since poor navigation burns time on the wrong things. This is that guide's view; other companies' rubrics may weight things differently, and the other three themes are still scored.

termDefinitions.meaning: 了解现行技术与公认模式，并能应用到问题上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Technical Excellence is knowing current technologies and recognized patterns and applying them to the problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能讲清概念、接住反馈、并与面试官协作解题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Communication and Collaboration means explaining ideas clearly, taking feedback, and collaborating with the interviewer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用核心概念解决拆出的子问题并拼成整体，即 Solution Design。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Solution Design means solving each subproblem with core concepts and assembling them into a coherent whole.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模糊问题拆解、排优先级并推进到解的能力，即 Problem Navigation。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem Navigation is the ability to decompose an ambiguous problem, prioritize it, and drive toward a solution.

optionExplanations: 误解：技术积累再多，遇到没见过的新题依然可能先卡在推进路径上。
误解：表达能力再强，拆解不出方案方向也没用。
误解：整合能力再强，方向一开始就错了，拼装也救不回来。
对，问题导航常是整场最重要、新手最容易栽的一环，决定先做什么、舍弃什么。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: no amount of technical depth helps if you're already stuck on how to move forward on an unfamiliar prompt.
Misconception: strong communication does not help if you never decompose the problem in the right direction.
Misconception: strong assembly skill cannot rescue a design if the direction was wrong from the start.
Right — problem navigation is often the single most important piece and where beginners most often trip up, deciding what to tackle first and what to skip.

scenario: 高级岗 45 分钟面试，你有 40 分钟都在讲 API 和表结构，没进入任何深挖。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute senior loop you spend 40 minutes on APIs and table schemas and never enter a deep dive.
q: 高级别候选人把大部分时间耗在基础环节、没进入任何深挖，会怎样？
q_en: What happens if a senior-level candidate spends most of the interview on basics and never reaches a deep dive?
options: 只要基础对就算达标
考官会主动延长时间
自动按中级标准重评
达不到该级别的深度预期
options_en: Getting the basics right is enough to pass.
The interviewer will proactively extend the time.
You get automatically re-evaluated by mid-level standards.
Falls short of the level's depth expectation.
why: 高级别的评分预期是快速过基础、把时间留给 deep dive 展示深度；全场耗在基础上等于没机会展示信号。
why_en: A senior candidate who spends the whole interview on basics never gets to show the depth expected at that level.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试中针对某个组件展开的深度追问环节，即英文说的 deep dive。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is the part of the interview where you go into depth on one specific component.

optionExplanations: 误解：基础正确只是门槛，高级候选人还要额外展示深度判断。
误解：面试时间通常固定，考官不会因为你慢就主动加时。
误解：评分通常按目标级别的信号来看，不会自动降档重评。
对，全场耗在基础上就没机会做深挖，等于没能展示这个级别该有的深度。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: correct basics are only the floor — senior candidates are also expected to show depth of judgment.
Misconception: interview time is usually fixed, so the interviewer won't add time just because you're slow.
Misconception: scoring looks for the target level's signal, it does not automatically downgrade to a lower bar.
Right — spending the whole interview on basics leaves no room for a deep dive, so the depth expected at that level never gets shown.

scenario: 题目是「设计限流器」，要求支撑百万级 QPS，你得决定白板上该画哪一类构件。
scenario_en: The prompt is "design a rate limiter" for a million QPS, and you must decide what kind of building blocks belong on the whiteboard.
q: 「设计 Uber」「设计限流器」这类题，典型要用到的构件是？
q_en: What building blocks do prompts like designing Uber or a rate limiter typically use?
options: 服务、负载均衡、数据库等构件
只靠前端客户端代码就能拼出方案

scenario: 白板上画好订单服务、库存服务、支付服务、数据库四个框，你逐个讲完各自职责就收尾，全程没说过一次下单请求在它们之间怎么流转。
scenario_en: Your whiteboard has four boxes — order service, inventory service, payment service, database — and you finish by describing each box's job, never once saying how a checkout request flows between them.
q: 这种「只讲组件、不讲组件间流转」的讲法会怎样拖垮方案设计评分？
q_en: How does describing only the boxes, never the flow between them, sink your solution design score?
options: 组件数量偏多，超出白板可画的范围
缺少伪代码，考官看不到方法级实现细节
选型偏旧过时，会被判在技术卓越这一维度上不达标
面试官拼不出端到端路径，追问接口就答不上
options_en: There are too many boxes to fit on the whiteboard.
Without pseudocode the interviewer can't see method-level detail.
The choices look dated, so you get marked down on the technical excellence dimension.
The interviewer can't trace an end-to-end path, so interface follow-ups go unanswered.
why: 方案设计考的是各块能否拼成连贯整体，而不是零件堆砌；只讲职责时考官无法验证任何一条端到端路径。代价是补接口要吃掉本该用于深挖的时间。
why_en: Solution design is judged on whether the pieces fit into a cohesive whole, so with only per-box duties the interviewer can't verify a single end-to-end path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 方案设计：用核心概念解决每块子问题，并让各块拼成连贯整体的评估维度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Solution Design is the dimension that judges whether you solve each subproblem and assemble the pieces into a cohesive whole.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个真实请求从入口穿过各个组件直到落库返回的完整链路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An end-to-end path is the full route one real request takes from entry through every component until it is stored and answered.

termDefinitions.meaning: 技术卓越：考察是否了解当前主流技术与公认模式并能用上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Technical Excellence is the dimension covering whether you know current technologies and recognized patterns and can apply them.

optionExplanations: 组件多寡不决定评分，四个框很常见；真正的问题是框之间没有连线语义。
系统设计轮不要求方法级伪代码，那是低层设计面试关心的粒度。
选型过时属于技术卓越维度的失分点，这里选型没问题，缺的是拼接。
对，考官只能看到四段独立职责，无法追踪一次下单怎么流过它们，任一接口追问都答不上。
optionExplanations_en: Box count doesn't drive the score — four is ordinary; what's missing is meaning on the arrows between them.
System design rounds don't ask for method-level pseudocode; that granularity belongs to low-level design.
Dated choices lose points under technical excellence — the choices here are fine, the assembly is what's absent.
Right — the interviewer sees four isolated duties and can't trace one checkout through them, so any interface probe goes unanswered.
